changes.text: When an app stops because its container got no network address, the Activity page now says so, with the reason Proxmox gave (DHCP failing at container start). Installing with a static IP address under Advanced options avoids DHCP altogether.

Apps that need the network the moment they start, such as Minecraft Server, no longer stop right after installing. Proxmox connects the network a few seconds after the app starts, so the installer now makes the app wait for it.

Every app in the store has been installed and started on a real Proxmox host. Apps that failed the test are hidden, and apps nobody has tested yet are marked Not tested. tools/compat.js runs the test for new apps.
When an app stops right after installing, the Activity page shows the last lines the app printed, so you can see why. This needs the file browser to be set up.

Downloaded images are removed from the host after an install. This needs one more right on the API role: run 'pveum role modify AppStore --privs Datastore.Allocate --append 1' once in the Proxmox host's shell.

Game server page for Minecraft Server (Java Edition): a live console with a command line, the players who are online with message, kick, ban, operator and game mode, plus the whitelist, ban list and operators.
Plugins tab for Minecraft: see, enable, disable and delete plugins, upload a .jar, and search and install from Modrinth. On Fabric and Forge servers it manages mods.
Settings tab for Minecraft with real fields: server name, max players, game mode, difficulty, PvP, whitelist, server type, version, memory, seed and EULA.
Upload button in the file browser, for files up to 64 MB.
The helper on the Proxmox host has a new version. If you use the file browser, open the Files tab once and run the command it shows.
One-command installer: a script for the Proxmox host that creates the container, installs the App Store and creates its API token. The setup page then only asks for a password.
The README's install guide is rewritten around the installer, with the manual steps kept as an alternative.

File browser on the Manage page: look through a running app's files, edit text files, download, rename, delete, and create files and folders. It needs a one-time setup on the Proxmox host, which the Files tab walks you through.
Shortcuts page: save links you want to keep, each with a name and notes.
Update button in the top bar when a newer version of the App Store is on GitHub. It shows what is new, and can install the update for you once set up (see Updating in the README).
The Manage page shows what the app uses right now: CPU, memory, disk and network traffic.
Manage now opens a full page for each app. Container settings: name, CPU cores, memory, swap, disk size, network bridge and IP address, start on boot.
App settings on the Manage page: change an app's environment variables and the port, path and HTTPS setting behind its Open button, then restart it in one go.
Manage button on every installed app and virtual machine: see its address, image and disk use, and change CPU cores, memory and start-on-boot.
Changelog page: see what changed in each version, right in the app.
Screenshots for 19 more apps. 182 of the 199 apps now have them; most of the rest are servers without a web page.
100 more apps in the store, 199 in total. Among them Pi-hole, Home Assistant, Jenkins, JupyterLab, Deluge, Duplicati, Guacamole, MySQL and MongoDB.
New category: Communication, with Element, Mumble and TeamSpeak.
Screenshots for 39 more of the original apps.
App details: click an app in the store to see a description, screenshots, the Docker image, its web port and a link to the source.
Advanced install options: choose the image version, container ID, storage, network bridge, a static IP address, swap, extra environment variables, and whether the app starts at boot.
Automatic updates: the App Store checks GitHub every minute and updates itself. A broken update is skipped and the working version keeps running.
My apps now shows apps and virtual machines in separate sections.
Step-by-step install guide in the README.
74 more apps in the store, 99 in total, including databases and a Minecraft server.
Apps that need a password or secret key get a random one filled in when you install them.
Apps without a web page show their IP address after installing instead of an Open button.
My apps: overview of all containers and virtual machines with status, CPU, memory and IP address, and buttons to start, stop, restart and delete.
Store: one-click install of 25 apps from Docker images, plus any custom image.
Activity: live progress for every install.
First-run setup that connects to Proxmox with a limited API token.
